question: Why does DNS normally run over UDP, and when does it have to use TCP instead?
answer_hinglish:
DNS ka normal case ek chhota question aur ek chhota answer hai, isliye UDP use hota hai: na handshake, na connection state, ek packet jaata hai aur ek wapas aata hai. TCP mein pehle 3-way handshake hota hai (ek extra round trip), phir connection close -- ek 40-50 byte ke query ke liye yeh bahut mehenga hai, aur server ko har client ka connection state yaad rakhna padta.

Lekin UDP ki do kamzoriyan hain. Pehli: bina EDNS ke DNS over UDP ka answer 512 bytes tak limited hai (RFC 1035). Bada answer aaye toh server TC=1 (truncated) bhejta hai aur client ko wahi query TCP par dobara karni padti hai. Doosri: UDP mein koi handshake nahi, toh source address forge karna aasaan hai -- spoofing ka poora problem yahin se aata hai. TCP par handshake peer ko prove kar deta hai.

Is project mein dono transports haath se likhe hain src/transport.ts mein. queryUdp har upstream query ka default raasta hai; Resolver.exchange reply mein header.tc dekhta hai aur true ho toh SAME server se queryTcp se poochta hai. TCP par har message ke aage 2-byte length prefix lagta hai (RFC 1035 4.2.2), kyunki TCP byte stream hai, message stream nahi. Stub server (src/server.ts) bhi UDP aur TCP dono ek hi port par sunta hai. Zone transfers (AXFR) bhi TCP par hote hain, par woh is project mein serve nahi hote -- NOTIMP milta hai.
why_needed: Interview mein yeh pehla sawaal hota hai; iske bina TC bit, spoofing aur 512-byte limit samajh nahi aate.
real_world_analogy: Postcard vs phone call: chhoti baat postcard (UDP) par likh do, sasta aur fast. Lambi baat ho toh phone (TCP) karna padta hai -- pehle number milao, hello bolo, phir baat.
how_it_works: Client query UDP par bhejta hai -> reply TC=0 toh done. TC=1 -> TCP connect -> 2-byte length + query -> 2-byte length + full reply -> close.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts mein queryUdp (fresh dgram socket, random port) aur queryTcp (net.connect, LengthPrefixedReader). src/resolver.ts Resolver.exchange TC dekh kar TCP retry karta hai. Test: resolver.test.ts 'a truncated (TC) UDP reply is retried over TCP to the same server' -- fake server ka log ['big.alpha.test 16 udp', 'big.alpha.test 16 tcp'] hona chahiye.
advantages: UDP: ek round trip, server par koi connection state nahi
TCP fallback se bade answers bhi aa jaate hain
disadvantages: UDP spoof karna aasaan hai
TC ke baad TCP ek poora extra round trip plus handshake leta hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki DNS 'sirf UDP' hai -- TCP support RFC 7766 ke hisaab se zaroori hai
TC=1 wale truncated answer ke records use kar lena
TCP par length prefix bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: EDNS(0) 512-byte limit ko kaise badhata hai?
TCP retry mein naya ID kyun liya gaya?
DNS over TLS / HTTPS kis transport par chalte hain?

question: What does the TC bit mean, where does the 512-byte limit come from, and what does the stub server do with a big answer?
answer_hinglish:
TC (truncated) header ka ek bit hai jo kehta hai: "yeh answer poora nahi hai, jo hai woh mat use karo, TCP par dobara poocho". 512 bytes RFC 1035 ki original limit hai DNS over UDP ke liye. EDNS(0) ek OPT record ke through client bata sakta hai ki woh bada UDP payload le sakta hai, par yeh project EDNS implement nahi karta, isliye dono taraf 512 hi limit hai.

Stub server mein yeh src/server.ts ke DnsServer.handle ke end mein hota hai. Pehle poora reply encode hota hai. Agar transport "udp" hai aur wire.length > UDP_MAX_ANSWER (512), toh counters.truncated++ hota hai, reply.header.tc = true set hota hai, answers aur authority khaali kar diye jaate hain, aur dobara encode hota hai. Question section rehta hai taaki client match kar sake. TCP par wahi answer poora jaata hai, kyunki wahan 2-byte length prefix hai (max 65535 bytes).

Resolver side par ulta kaam hai: upstream reply mein TC=1 dikha toh Resolver.exchange same server se queryTcp karta hai. Test server.test.ts 'an answer over 512 bytes is truncated on UDP (TC=1, no records) and complete over TCP' big.alpha.test TXT (30 chunks, BIG_TXT) se dono cheezein check karta hai. Mutation S2 (big UDP answers not truncated) ko 2 tests ne pakda, aur R1 (TC bit ignored) ko 3 ne. Interop mein nslookup -vc se bhi yahi TXT TCP par aaya.
why_needed: Bina TC handling ke bade answers (lambe TXT, bahut saare A records) ya toh kat jaate ya IP fragmentation mein kho jaate.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein bada order: waiter kehta hai 'itna ek plate mein nahi aayega, counter se poora parcel le lo' -- aadhi plate nahi deta.
how_it_works: encode -> length > 512 aur UDP? -> tc=true, answers=[], authority=[] -> encode again. Client TC dekhta hai -> TCP par same query.
in_this_project: src/server.ts: UDP_MAX_ANSWER = 512, handle() ka last block, counters.truncated. src/resolver.ts exchange mein reply.header.tc check. test/fixtures.ts ka BIG_TXT. Tests: server.test.ts TC test, resolver.test.ts TC retry test, interop.test.ts '-vc (TCP) gets the big TXT record that does not fit in 512 bytes of UDP'.
advantages: Simple aur RFC ke hisaab se sahi
Client kabhi aadha answer use nahi karta
disadvantages: Bina EDNS ke kaafi answers bevajah TCP par jaate hain
Records ko trim karke fit karne ki koshish nahi hoti (RFC allow karta hai)
common_mistakes: TC=1 ke saath kuch records bhej dena aur client ka unhe use kar lena
TCP reply par bhi 512 limit laga dena
Question section bhi hata dena
follow_up_questions: EDNS(0) implement karoge toh limit kahan se aayegi?
Kya truncated reply mein kuch records rakhna allowed hai?

question: How does LengthPrefixedReader turn a TCP byte stream into DNS messages, and why is it shared by client and server?
answer_hinglish:
TCP par DNS message ke aage uski length 2 bytes big-endian mein aati hai (RFC 1035 4.2.2). Problem yeh hai ki TCP 'data' event message boundaries nahi jaanta: ek chunk mein aadha message ho sakta hai, do poore messages, ya length ka sirf pehla byte. LengthPrefixedReader isi ko handle karta hai.

feed(chunk) bache hue buffer ke saath naya chunk jodta hai (buffer khaali ho toh concat skip). Phir loop: jab tak kam se kam 2 bytes hain, readUInt16BE(0) se len padho; agar buffer mein 2 + len bytes nahi hain toh break aur wait karo; warna frame nikalo aur aage badho. Ek feed se zero, ek ya kai frames nikal sakte hain. Frame Buffer.from se COPY hota hai, taaki bade receive buffer ka reference na atke. pending getter batata hai kitne bytes adhure pade hain.

Ulta kaam frameTcp karta hai: 2-byte length + message. Dono src/transport.ts mein hain aur teen jagah use hote hain: client side queryTcp, stub server ka DnsServer.onTcp, aur test helper (server.test.ts tcpExchange, fakenet). Ek hi implementation matlab framing bug ek jagah fix hota hai. Server test 'TCP: several pipelined queries on one connection, the last split across writes' saare frames ek write mein bhejta hai aur last ke 3 bytes 20 ms baad -- yeh reader ke dono raste (multiple frames ek chunk mein, aur split frame) chala deta hai.

Ek honest note: reader mein max length check alag se nahi hai, par 2-byte length khud 65535 par cap hai, aur server ka tcpIdleMs adhure frames wale idle connection ko band karta hai.
why_needed: Bina framing ke TCP par pehla split packet hi stream desync kar dega aur har aage ka message galat padha jayega.
real_world_analogy: Train ke dibbe: har dibbe par likha hai kitni seats hain. Platform par aadha dibba aaya toh aap wait karte ho, ginti pe bharosa karte ho, aage wale ka andaza nahi lagate.
how_it_works: feed: buf = buf + chunk -> while buf.length >= 2: len = u16be(buf) -> buf.length < 2+len ? break : out.push(copy(buf[2..2+len])), buf = rest -> return out.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts: LengthPrefixedReader (feed, pending), frameTcp, queryTcp mein use. src/server.ts onTcp har socket ke liye naya reader banata hai. Test: server.test.ts 'TCP: several pipelined queries on one connection, the last split across writes'.
advantages: Split aur coalesced chunks dono sahi
Client, server aur tests ek hi code use karte hain
Frame copy se memory retention nahi
disadvantages: Har adhure chunk par Buffer.concat -- bahut chhote chunks mein quadratic ho sakta hai (DNS ke 64 KB tak ke messages mein typically chalta hai)
Zero-length frame bhi ek frame ban jaata hai; decode use reject karta hai
common_mistakes: Ek 'data' event ko ek message maan lena
Length padhne se pehle 2 bytes hone ka check bhool jaana
frameTcp mein length little-endian likhna
follow_up_questions: Is reader ke liye byte-by-byte feeding ka test kaise likhoge?
65535 se bada message ho toh kya hoga?

question: Walk through matchesQuery: which checks decide that a reply really answers our query, and why each one?
answer_hinglish:
matchesQuery(reply, query) src/transport.ts mein hai aur UDP aur TCP dono paths use karte hain. Woh true tabhi deta hai jab:

1. reply.header.qr true hai -- yeh response hai, kisi aur ka query nahi.
2. reply.header.id === query.header.id -- 16-bit random ID echo hua.
3. Dono taraf pehla question maujood hai aur reply mein EXACTLY ek question hai (reply.questions.length !== 1 toh false).
4. type aur class same hain, aur naam sameName se match hota hai.

Har check attacker ke liye ek aur cheez guess karne layak banata hai. ID check ke bina off-path attacker ko sirf port guess karna hai. Question check ke bina ek genuine-looking reply jo kisi DOOSRE naam ka answer de (evil.alpha.test), woh hamare query ka answer maan liya jaata. Exactly-one-question rule weird replies ko reject karta hai jinmein extra questions chhupe hon.

sameName canonicalName par based hai -- ASCII case-insensitive. Yeh zaroori hai kyunki servers question ko case badal kar echo kar sakte hain aur DNS names case-insensitive hain. Iska ek side effect: 0x20 randomisation (case bits se extra entropy) is project mein nahi hai, kyunki uske liye exact-case compare chahiye hota.

Source address/port check matchesQuery mein nahi, queryUdp ke message handler mein pehle hota hai (rinfo se). Mutations: T1 (ID check hataya) aur T3 (question check hataya) dono ek-ek test ne pakde -- 'a reply with the wrong ID is ignored, the real one is used' aur 'a reply that echoes a different question is ignored'.
why_needed: Galat reply accept karna matlab cache poisoning; yeh function poisoning ke khilaaf pehli deewar hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier se parcel lete waqt order number, aapka naam aur item -- teeno match karo. Sirf 'parcel aaya hai' sun kar mat le lo.
how_it_works: qr? -> id equal? -> q aur r exist, r count 1? -> type, class, sameName(name) -> true. Koi bhi fail -> false -> caller ignore karta hai (UDP) ya fail karta hai (TCP).
in_this_project: src/transport.ts matchesQuery; src/wire.ts sameName (canonicalName ke upar). queryUdp mismatch par onIgnored('mismatch') bulata hai; queryTcp TransportError deta hai. Tests resolver.test.ts ke 'resolver: spoofing and cache-poisoning defences' block mein.
advantages: Pure function, socket ke bina test ho sakti hai
UDP aur TCP dono ek hi rule follow karte hain
disadvantages: Case-insensitive compare 0x20 entropy ka raasta band karta hai
Ek bhi question na echo karne wale (kuch purane) servers ke replies reject ho jaate
common_mistakes: Sirf ID check karna
Naam ko plain string === se compare karna (case issue)
Source check ko yahin daalna jabki woh rinfo se aata hai
follow_up_questions: 0x20 randomisation add karne ke liye yeh function kaise badlega?
TCP par mismatch ko ignore kyun nahi karte?

question: How do the random source port and random query ID make spoofing harder, and how much do they add?
answer_hinglish:
UDP mein handshake nahi hai, toh koi bhi packet par hamare upstream server ka source address likh kar bhej sakta hai. Off-path attacker hamari query dekh nahi sakta, isliye use reply ko acceptable banane wali cheezein GUESS karni padti hain: 16-bit ID aur woh source port jis par hum sun rahe hain. Fixed port ho toh sirf ID bachta hai -- 65536 values, jo race mein jeeta ja sakta hai.

Is project mein har UDP query ke liye queryUdp ek NAYA dgram socket banata hai aur bindRandom se use crypto.randomInt(SOURCE_PORT_MIN, 65536) port par bind karta hai -- matlab 10000-65535, README ke hisaab se lagbhag 55000 values. ID randomId() se aata hai: randomInt(0, 0x10000). Dono milakar README lagbhag 3.6 billion combinations per query batata hai, 65536 ki jagah. crypto.randomInt use hota hai, Math.random nahi, kyunki Math.random predictable PRNG hai.

Iske upar do aur filters: reply EXACT address aur port se aana chahiye jahan bheja tha (rinfo check, warna 'wrong-source'), aur matchesQuery (QR, ID, question). Galat reply ignore hota hai, query khatam nahi hoti.

Test 'query IDs and source ports are random' 20 lookups karta hai aur check karta hai ki kam se kam 18 alag IDs aur 18 alag ports hain aur har port >= 10000. Mutations T4 (fixed source port) aur T5 (fixed query ID) dono isi test ne pakde. Honest limit: yeh sirf guessing mehenga banata hai; asli fix DNSSEC hai, jo implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Kaminsky style attack mein attacker bahut saari races khel sakta hai; entropy hi decide karti hai ki ek race jeetne ka chance kitna hai.
real_world_analogy: Locker ka combination: sirf 4 digit ka lock (ID) jaldi toot jaata hai. Doosra 5 digit ka dial (port) jod do toh dono saath guess karne padte hain.
how_it_works: per query: port = randomInt(10000, 65536), id = randomInt(0, 65536) -> send -> har aane wala packet: source check -> decode -> matchesQuery -> sab pass toh accept, warna ignore.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts: randomId, SOURCE_PORT_MIN, bindRandom, queryUdp. src/resolver.ts exchange har query ke liye randomId() leta hai. Test: resolver.test.ts 'query IDs and source ports are random' (fakenet log mein id aur port record hota hai).
advantages: Har query par lagbhag 3.6 billion combinations (README ka estimate)
CSPRNG, predictable nahi
Port aur ID dono tested
disadvantages: Har query ek socket bind -- system calls ka kharcha
On-path attacker (jo traffic dekh sakta hai) ke khilaaf kuch nahi karta
common_mistakes: Math.random se ID banana
Ek long-lived socket sab queries ke liye (fixed port)
Randomness ko 'test nahi ho sakta' maan kar test hi na likhna
follow_up_questions: Port OS par chhod dete toh kya problem thi?
NAT ke peeche random port ka kya hota hai?
On-path attacker ke khilaaf kya karoge?

question: Explain the Kaminsky attack and why the bailiwick rule is a security control, not just a correctness rule.
answer_hinglish:
Classic cache poisoning mein attacker ko wait karna padta tha ki bank.test ka cached record expire ho, phir ek race. Haare toh agla mauka TTL ke baad. Kaminsky (2008) ne yeh wait khatam kar diya: attacker resolver se random, non-existent naam puchwata hai -- x1.bank.test, x2.bank.test -- har ek cache miss hai, toh har ek ek fresh race hai. Uske forged replies mein fake answer ke saath ek referral bhi hota hai: "bank.test is served by ns.bank.test at <attacker address>", glue ke saath. Ek race jeet gaya toh poori zone uski, jab tak TTL hai.

Isliye defence do layers mein hai. Pehli: race jeetna mehenga banao -- random port + random ID (lagbhag 3.6 billion combinations), exact source aur exact question. Doosri: agar koi forged ya bas malicious reply andar aa bhi gaya, toh woh sirf USI zone ke records sikha sake jiske liye humne poocha tha. Yeh bailiwick hai: zone Z ka server sirf Z ya uske neeche ke records sikha sakta hai; glue tabhi use/cache hota hai jab woh referral bhejne wale server ki zone ke andar ho. Aur referral data (NS, glue) ranking mein answer se neeche hai -- kabhi unexpired answer ko overwrite nahi karta.

Is project mein bailiwick filter Resolver.classify mein hai. Test 'bailiwick: extra answer and additional records for ANOTHER zone are not cached' alpha.test ke server se www.beta.test, ns.hoster.example aur beta.test NS inject karta hai; trace mein 'dropped 3 out-of-bailiwick' aana chahiye. Mutation R2 (bailiwick off) 2 tests ne pakda. Real data par bhi dikha: gmail.com MX trace mein 10 *.l.google.com address records drop hue.
why_needed: Bailiwick ke bina ek compromised ya malicious authoritative server kisi bhi doosri zone ko poison kar sakta hai, bina koi race jeete.
real_world_analogy: Society ka guard sirf apni building ke flats ke baare mein bata sakta hai. Agar woh kahe 'saamne wali building ka watchman main hoon', toh aap nahi maanoge.
how_it_works: Attacker: random subdomain query trigger -> resolver upstream bhejta hai -> attacker flood of forged replies (guessing port+ID) jinmein referral + glue. Defence: guessing fail (entropy, exact checks) + classify mein out-of-zone records drop + Rank se referral data answer ko replace nahi karta.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts queryUdp/matchesQuery (race layer), src/resolver.ts classify (bailiwick layer), src/cache.ts Rank (referral < answer). Tests resolver.test.ts: 'bailiwick: extra answer and additional records for ANOTHER zone are not cached', 'bailiwick: out-of-zone glue in a referral is not used; the NS name is resolved properly'.
advantages: Ek jeeti hui race ka damage ek zone tak simit
Malicious-but-genuine server ke khilaaf bhi kaam karta hai
disadvantages: Out-of-bailiwick records drop hone se kabhi extra lookups lagte hain (gmail.com case)
Zone ke andar ka forged record bailiwick nahi rokta -- sirf DNSSEC
common_mistakes: Additional section ka har A record cache kar lena
Bailiwick ko string endsWith se check karna
Referral glue ko answer ki tarah client ko de dena
follow_up_questions: Bailiwick zone ke ANDAR ke forged record ke khilaaf kya karta hai?
RFC 5452 aur kya suggest karta hai?
Random subdomain attack ko rate limit se kaise rokoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Bailiwick strict hai: kabhi kabhi ek legitimate out-of-zone record bhi drop hota hai aur dobara resolve karna padta hai. Extra queries ki keemat par poisoning ka blast radius chhota hota hai -- yeh trade worth it hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar attacker race jeet le AUR forged record zone ke andar ho (x1.bank.test ke liye bank.test ka NS), toh bailiwick allow karega -- yahin port/ID entropy aur DNSSEC kaam aate hain.
advanced.alternatives: DNSSEC validation (cryptographic proof), 0x20 case randomisation, DNS cookies (RFC 7873), aur suspicious mismatch rate dekh kar TCP par switch karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x queries par race opportunities bhi utni hi badhti hain. Production resolvers mismatched replies count karte hain aur threshold par us zone ke liye TCP force karte hain; yahan onIgnored hook ek metric ke liye ready hai, par action nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: onIgnored ko per-server counter mein badlo, spikes par alert; DNSSEC validation; 0x20; aage chal kar referral NS sets ko child zone se re-verify karna (revalidation).

question: Random ports and IDs only make spoofing expensive. Why is DNSSEC the real fix, and what would adding it to this resolver involve?
answer_hinglish:
Random port aur ID probability ka khel hai: attacker ko lagbhag 3.6 billion combinations mein se guess karna hai, par bahut saari races aur fast link ke saath chance zero nahi hota. Aur on-path attacker (jo hamara traffic dekh sakta hai, jaise compromised router) ke liye entropy ka koi matlab hi nahi -- woh ID aur port seedha padh leta hai. DNSSEC alag level par kaam karta hai: zone owner apne RRsets par signature (RRSIG) lagata hai, parent zone child ki key ka hash (DS) sign karta hai, aur yeh chain root ki trust anchor key tak jaati hai. Forged record ke paas valid signature nahi hoga, chahe woh race jeet le.

Is project mein DNSSEC implement nahi hai -- README ki NOT implemented list mein pehla item. DS/RRSIG jaise types wire.ts mein raw rdata ki tarah decode hote hain (RFC 3597), aur hum OPT/DO bit bhejte hi nahi, toh servers signatures bhejenge bhi nahi.

Add karne ke liye: (1) EDNS(0) pehle -- DO bit ke bina signatures nahi aate, aur signed answers 512 bytes se bade hote hain, toh UDP buffer size badhana padega; (2) DNSKEY, RRSIG, DS, NSEC/NSEC3 ke parsers; (3) RRset ka canonical form (lowercase names, sorted rdata) -- yeh exactly woh hai jo hum abhi case-insensitive compression mein bigaad dete hain, isliye signing input alag se banana padega; (4) RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519 verification (node:crypto se ho sakta hai, zero-dependency rule nahi tootega); (5) root trust anchor as data, root-hints.ts jaisa; (6) negative answers ke liye NSEC/NSEC3 proofs; (7) cache mein validation status (secure/insecure/bogus).
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap jaante ho ki entropy defences 'mitigation' hain, 'fix' nahi, aur DNSSEC ka cost kya hai.
real_world_analogy: Entropy ek bheed mein aapka chehra pehchanne jaisa hai -- dhokha ho sakta hai. DNSSEC sarkari stamp wala ID card hai: nakli banane ke liye signing key chahiye.
how_it_works: Trust anchor (root DNSKEY) -> root zone DS for 'test' signed -> test DNSKEY match -> test zone DS for alpha.test -> alpha.test DNSKEY -> RRSIG over www.alpha.test A verify -> secure. Kahin chain toote -> bogus -> SERVFAIL.
in_this_project: Implement nahi hai. Abhi defences: src/transport.ts (port, ID, matchesQuery), src/resolver.ts classify (bailiwick). src/wire.ts unknown types ko RAW rakhta hai, isliye DS/RRSIG decode crash nahi karte. README 'What it does NOT do (and what really closes the hole): DNSSEC validation.'
advantages: Cryptographic guarantee, probability nahi
On-path attacker ke khilaaf bhi kaam karta hai
disadvantages: Bahut complex: canonical form, key rollover, NSEC3, algorithms
Bade responses, zyada TCP
Kai zones abhi bhi unsigned hain -- unke liye koi protection nahi
common_mistakes: Sochna ki random port se spoofing 'solve' ho gaya
DNSSEC ko encryption samajhna -- yeh sirf authenticity deta hai, privacy nahi (woh DoT/DoH ka kaam hai)
Validation fail par answer phir bhi de dena
follow_up_questions: Bogus answer par client ko kya rcode doge?
Unsigned zone ke liye kya hota hai?
DoT/DoH DNSSEC se kya alag solve karte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: DNSSEC correctness deta hai par CPU (signature verify), bandwidth (bade replies) aur code complexity mehenga hai. Hamare jaise learning resolver mein pehle wire format, resolution aur cache sahi karna priority tha; DNSSEC bina EDNS ke shuru bhi nahi ho sakta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Clock skew se valid signatures 'expired' lagte hain; key rollover mein galti poori zone ko bogus kar deti hai; NSEC3 hashing ka bug saare negative answers tod deta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Kisi validating upstream (forwarder) par bharosa karna aur AD bit padhna -- simple par trust shift ho jaata hai; ya DoT/DoH se ek trusted resolver tak channel secure karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Validation results bhi cache karne padenge (DNSKEY, DS sets), warna har query par poori chain verify hogi. Signature verification CPU ka bada hissa banti hai high QPS par.
advanced.production_improvements: EDNS(0) -> DO bit -> parsers -> canonical form -> verify -> negative proofs -> cache mein validation state; har step ke liye RFC test vectors aur mutation checks, jaise is project ki W/T/R tables.

question: Why does queryUdp ignore a bad reply and keep waiting, while queryTcp fails immediately on a mismatch?
answer_hinglish:
UDP par galat reply aane ka matlab hamesha 'server toota hai' nahi hota -- woh ek attacker ka guess ho sakta hai, ya kisi purani query ka late reply. Agar pehla galat reply query khatam kar de (reject), toh attacker ko race jeetni bhi nahi padti: woh sirf garbage bhej kar har lookup fail kar sakta hai, ya hume next server par dhakel sakta hai. Isliye queryUdp ke message handler mein har fail case 'return opts.onIgnored?.(reason)' hai -- wrong-source, undecodable, mismatch -- aur socket sunta rehta hai jab tak genuine reply aaye ya timeout ho.

TCP par situation alag hai. Connection 3-way handshake ke baad bana hai, toh off-path attacker us stream mein bytes inject nahi kar sakta (sequence numbers guess karne padenge). Agar TCP par mismatched ya undecodable reply aaya, toh woh server khud broken hai. Wait karne ka koi fayda nahi, isliye queryTcp TransportError (ya WireError) se finish karta hai, aur askZone usko catch karke zone ka next server try karta hai. Code ka comment yahi kehta hai: "a mismatch is still a broken server: fail this server instead of using its answer."

Ek detail: garbage reply wale test ('a garbage reply from the right server is ignored and the query times out to the next server') mein ignored list mein 'undecodable' aata hai aur resolver timeout ke baad ALPHA2 se answer leta hai. Trade-off: ek broken UDP server poora timeoutMs (default 2000 ms) khaata hai, turant fail nahi hota.
why_needed: Fail-fast har jagah achha nahi hota; adversarial input par 'fail' khud ek attack surface ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Phone par koi kahe 'main bank se bol raha hoon' aur details galat hon, toh aap call kaat kar asli call ka intezaar karte ho -- apna account band nahi karwa dete. Par bank branch ke counter par (TCP, verified jagah) galat jawab mile toh manager ke paas jaate ho.
how_it_works: UDP: message -> check fail -> onIgnored(reason) -> keep listening -> timer fire -> TimeoutError -> next server. TCP: frame -> decode/match fail -> finish(TransportError) -> askZone catch -> next server.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts queryUdp (IgnoreReason: 'wrong-source' | 'undecodable' | 'mismatch', UdpOptions.onIgnored) aur queryTcp. src/resolver.ts askZone TimeoutError/TransportError/WireError par continue. Tests resolver.test.ts: 'a reply with the wrong ID is ignored, the real one is used', 'a garbage reply from the right server is ignored...'.
advantages: Attacker cheap failures nahi kar sakta
TCP par broken server jaldi chhoot jaata hai
onIgnored se visibility milti hai
disadvantages: Broken UDP server poora timeout khaata hai
Bahut saare forged packets bhi socket par process hote hain (CPU)
common_mistakes: Pehle galat UDP reply par reject karna
TCP par bhi wait karte rehna
Ignored replies ko silently drop karna bina kisi counter ke
follow_up_questions: Ignored replies ki ginti badhe toh resolver ko kya karna chahiye?
Late genuine reply kisi naye socket par aaye toh kya hota hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ignore-and-wait security ke liye sahi hai par latency mehengi: ek garbage-bhejne wala server har baar timeoutMs le leta hai. TCP par trust zyada hai isliye fail-fast sasta aur sahi hai.

question: Why does bindRandom pick the source port itself instead of letting the OS choose, and how does it handle a port that is taken?
answer_hinglish:
Port 0 par bind karo toh OS ek ephemeral port deta hai. Kai OS mein yeh range chhoti hoti hai ya allocation predictable (sequential) ho sakti hai, aur hamare paas iska koi control ya guarantee nahi. Spoofing defence ka poora point yeh hai ki port attacker ke liye unpredictable ho, toh PLAN.md ka decision hai: port hum khud crypto.randomInt(SOURCE_PORT_MIN, 65536) se chunte hain -- 10000 se 65535. SOURCE_PORT_MIN 10000 isliye ki usse neeche well-known aur registered ports hain jo zyada busy hote hain.

Random port kabhi kabhi already taken hoga (koi aur process, ya hamari hi doosri in-flight query). bindRandom 8 attempts tak try karta hai: har baar naya dgram.createSocket('udp4'), 'error' event par listener, bind(pick()). Bind success toh error listener hata kar socket return. Fail toh socket close (try/catch, kyunki failed bind ke baad socket already closed ho sakta hai) aur naya port. 8 baar fail toh TransportError("could not bind a random UDP source port"), jise askZone baaki transport errors ki tarah handle karta hai.

Fresh socket per query hai, toh ek query ka port doosri query ke replies nahi sunta. UdpOptions.pickPort sirf tests ke liye override hai. Test 'query IDs and source ports are random' 20 queries mein kam se kam 18 alag ports maangta hai. Mutation T4 (fixed source port) isi ne pakda.
why_needed: Port entropy tabhi hai jab hum usse control karein; OS ka behaviour platform par depend karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Parking mein khud random spot chunna, attendant ke 'agla khaali' ke bharose nahi -- warna har koi andaza laga lega aap kahan ho.
how_it_works: for attempt < 8: sock = createSocket; await bind(pick()) -> ok ? return sock : close, retry. Phir throw TransportError.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts bindRandom, SOURCE_PORT_MIN, UdpOptions.pickPort, queryUdp. Test resolver.test.ts 'query IDs and source ports are random' (log.every(port >= 10000)).
advantages: Platform-independent entropy
Taken port ek normal case hai, error nahi
Tests ke liye injectable picker
disadvantages: Har query ek extra bind system call
Bahut busy machine par 8 attempts bhi fail ho sakte hain
common_mistakes: Port 0 par bind karke maan lena ki random hoga
Failed bind ke baad socket close na karna (leak)
Error listener hataana bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: NAT ke peeche yeh random port bachta hai kya?
IPv6 support add karte waqt bindRandom kya badlega?

question: How does the CLI in src/index.ts choose between serving and a one-off resolve, and how does it validate its settings?
answer_hinglish:
src/index.ts do modes deta hai. 'node dist/index.js resolve <name> [type]' ek baar root se resolve karta hai, har step print karta hai (trace console.log par), phir rcode, upstream queries ki ginti, time aur records print karke exit. Bina argument ke woh stub server chalata hai HOST:PORT par (UDP + TCP). Koi aur command ho toh error aur exit 2.

Settings environment variables se aate hain: HOST (default 127.0.0.1), PORT (5300), TIMEOUT_MS (2000), TRACE=1, ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1. intEnv() khaali ya missing par default deta hai, aur value /^\d+$/ match na kare toh message ke saath process.exit(2) -- 'abc' ya '-1' chupchap NaN nahi bante. parseType() A, MX jaise naam TYPE table mein dhoondhta hai, ya RFC 3597 style TYPEnnn (65536 se kam) leta hai; warna supported types ki list ke saath exit 2. resolve mode naam ka trailing dot hata deta hai, kyunki project ke andar names bina trailing dot ke rakhe jaate hain.

Serve mode mein loopback guard DnsServer.listen se PEHLE bhi lagta hai: !isLoopback(host) aur ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK !== '1' toh clear message aur exit 2. Listen ke baad JSON log line {event:'listening', host, port} aur ek hint ki Windows nslookup -port ignore karta hai. SIGINT/SIGTERM par stats() ke counters ke saath 'stopping' line log hoti hai aur server.close() hota hai.
why_needed: CLI pehli cheez hai jo user chalata hai; galat config par fail-fast aur saaf message debugging bachata hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM machine: card daalo (command), PIN galat format mein ho toh wahin mana -- paise nikalne ke beech mein nahi.
how_it_works: argv[2] == 'resolve' ? Resolver(trace=console.log).resolve -> print -> exit : cmd undefined ? loopback guard -> DnsServer.listen -> log : error exit 2.
in_this_project: src/index.ts: intEnv, parseType, resolve branch, loopback guard, stop() with server.stats(). README 'Run it' section mein commands aur settings.
advantages: Zero dependency -- koi CLI library nahi
Galat config start par hi pakdi jaati hai
Stop par stats ek JSON line mein
disadvantages: PORT ki 65535 upper limit intEnv check nahi karta (bind khud fail karega)
Ek hi resolver/cache poori process mein, config reload nahi
common_mistakes: Number(raw) seedha use karna (NaN ya negative chal jaata)
Loopback guard sirf library mein rakhna aur CLI mein stack trace dikhana
Trailing dot ke saath naam aage bhej dena
follow_up_questions: PORT=53 Windows par admin rights maangta hai kya?
resolve mode ka trace kis option se aata hai?

question: What is an open resolver, why is it an amplification weapon, and how does this project guard against becoming one?
answer_hinglish:
Open resolver woh recursive DNS server hai jo internet par kisi ki bhi query ka jawab deta hai. Problem: UDP mein source address forge ho sakta hai. Attacker victim ka IP source mein likh kar chhoti query bhejta hai, aur resolver bada answer VICTIM ko bhejta hai. server.ts ka comment kehta hai: ek 60-byte spoofed query kai guna bada reply trigger kar sakti hai. Hazaron open resolvers milakar victim par traffic ki baadh -- yeh DNS amplification DDoS hai. Saath mein strangers aapke cache par poisoning experiments bhi kar sakte hain.

Yeh stub server ek open recursive resolver hi hai: rate limiting nahi, access control nahi. Isliye default 127.0.0.1 par bind hota hai aur kuch aur bind karna explicitly opt-in hai. Guard do jagah hai: DnsServer.listen mein -- !isLoopback(host) && !allowNonLoopback toh Error 'refusing to bind ...'; aur src/index.ts mein listen se pehle bhi, ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1 na ho toh exit 2. isLoopback 127.0.0.1, ::1, 'localhost' aur 127.x.x.x (regex) ko loopback maanta hai; 0.0.0.0 loopback NAHI hai (woh saare interfaces hai).

Test 'refuses a non-loopback address unless allowNonLoopback is set' 0.0.0.0 par listen() reject hona check karta hai, aur isLoopback ke cases (127.0.0.53 true, 10.0.0.1 false, 0.0.0.0 false). Mutation S1 (non-loopback bind allowed) isi test ne pakda. README saaf kehta hai: ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK sirf private network par, kabhi public address nahi.
why_needed: Galti se 0.0.0.0 par chala diya gaya resolver kuch ghanton mein abuse ho sakta hai aur aapka IP blacklists mein jaa sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ke bahar free photocopy machine rakh dena jisme koi bhi kisi ke bhi naam se 1000 copies uske ghar bhijwa sake.
how_it_works: Attacker: src=victim, small query -> open resolver -> big reply -> victim. Guard: listen(host) -> isLoopback? ok : allowNonLoopback? ok : throw.
in_this_project: src/server.ts isLoopback aur DnsServer.listen; src/index.ts mein duplicate guard aur ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK env; header comment mein reason. Test server.test.ts 'stub server: bind guard'.
advantages: Safe by default
Library aur CLI dono level par guard
Explicit, naam se samajh aane wala opt-in
disadvantages: Loopback hi allowed hai, LAN par chalane ke liye poora guard band ho jaata hai -- beech ka ACL option nahi
Rate limiting ab bhi nahi hai
common_mistakes: 0.0.0.0 ko 'local' samajhna
Sirf firewall par bharosa karna
Amplification ko sirf bandwidth problem samajhna -- victim koi aur hai
follow_up_questions: Response Rate Limiting (RRL) kaise kaam karta hai?
Allowlist of client subnets kaise add karoge?
TCP par amplification kyun nahi hota?

question: Walk through DnsServer.handle: in what order does it reject packets, and why does each case get drop, FORMERR or NOTIMP?
answer_hinglish:
handle(buf, transport) ek query leta hai aur reply ka Buffer ya undefined (kuch mat bhejo) deta hai. Order bahut soch kar rakha hai:

1. decodeHeader fail (12 bytes se kam) -> DROP. ID hi nahi pata toh reply kisko match hoga? counters.dropped++.
2. header.qr true -> DROP. Yeh response hai, query nahi; jawab dene se do servers ping-pong mein phas sakte hain.
3. decodeMessage fail (WireError) -> FORMERR, SAME ID ke saath, questions khaali. Header padh liya tha, toh client ko bata sakte hain ki packet kharab hai.
4. opcode QUERY nahi (jaise STATUS) -> NOTIMP.
5. Zero ya ek se zyada questions -> FORMERR.
6. Class IN nahi (CHAOS jaisa 'version.bind') ya META_TYPES (AXFR 252, IXFR 251, MAILB, MAILA, ANY) -> NOTIMP. Zone transfer aur ANY serve nahi hote -- ANY amplification mein bhi popular hai.
7. Warna resolver.resolve(q.name, q.type), aur reply.

Har reply base() se banta hai: ID copy, QR=1, opcode copy, AA=0 (hum authoritative nahi), RD client ka copy, RA=1 (recursion available), rcode. Answers aur authority (negative ke liye SOA) resolver se aate hain. Client ka EDNS OPT ignore hota hai aur reply ke additional mein kuch nahi jaata -- test 'a query with an EDNS OPT record in additional is still answered (the OPT is ignored)'.

Tests server.test.ts mein har case: 'garbage with a readable header gets FORMERR with the same ID; less than a header gets nothing', QR test, 'other opcodes, other classes and ANY/AXFR get NOTIMP; zero or two questions get FORMERR'. Mutations S3, S4, S5 (ID copy hataya -- 4 tests fail), S6 sab pakde gaye.
why_needed: Server untrusted bytes leta hai; har galat input ka ek tay jawab hona chahiye jo na crash kare na loop banaye.
real_world_analogy: Post office counter: lifafa phata hai aur naam bhi nahi dikhta -> phenk do. Naam dikhta hai par form galat -> 'form galat hai' likh kar wapas. Aisi service maangi jo hum dete hi nahi -> 'yeh service nahi hai'.
how_it_works: decodeHeader -> qr? -> decodeMessage -> opcode -> question count -> class/type -> resolve -> base(rcode,[q]) + answers + authority -> TC check (UDP).
in_this_project: src/server.ts DnsServer.handle, META_TYPES, ServerStats counters (dropped, formerr, notimp, servfail, truncated). src/wire.ts decodeHeader alag function hai taaki body kharab ho tab bhi ID mile. Tests: test/server.test.ts 'stub server' block.
advantages: Har case ka tay rcode aur counter
Header aur body alag decode -- kharab body par bhi same-ID FORMERR
Loops aur ANY abuse band
disadvantages: OPT ignore karne se client ko pata nahi chalta ki EDNS support nahi hai (RFC 6891 FORMERR/BADVERS ka raasta hai)
NOTIMP ke liye bhi poora decode hota hai
common_mistakes: Kharab body par drop karna (client timeout tak wait karega)
QR=1 packets ka jawab dena
Reply mein AA=1 set karna jabki hum recursive hain
follow_up_questions: Client ne RD=0 bheja toh kya hona chahiye?
ANY ko NOTIMP ki jagah RFC 8482 ka minimal answer kyun nahi?

question: What could go wrong if the stub server answered packets that have QR=1, and how is that prevented and tested?
answer_hinglish:
QR bit batata hai ki packet query (0) hai ya response (1). Agar server har packet ka jawab de, response ka bhi, toh ek simple failure banta hai: server A ek response server B ko bhejta hai (ya attacker source forge karke A ka response B ko pahunchata hai), B use 'query' samajh kar response bhejta hai, A phir jawab deta hai -- infinite ping-pong. Dono servers ka CPU aur bandwidth jalta hai, bina kisi client ke. Spoofed source ke saath attacker ek hi packet se yeh loop shuru kar sakta hai.

Is project mein DnsServer.handle ka doosra check yahi hai: decodeHeader ke turant baad 'if (header.qr) { this.counters.dropped++; return undefined; }'. Koi reply nahi, koi error nahi, sirf counter. Isse pehle ka check (header bhi nahi padh paaye) bhi drop hai, kyunki bina ID ke reply kisi kaam ka nahi.

Test 'a packet with QR=1 (a response) is dropped, so two servers can never ping-pong' buildQuery se query banata hai, header.qr = true karta hai aur 300 ms mein reply undefined expect karta hai. Mutation S3 (packets with QR=1 answered) isi test ne pakda. Resolver side par ulta rule hai: matchesQuery sirf QR=1 wale replies accept karta hai, toh koi query hamare upstream socket par answer nahi maani jaati.
why_needed: Do machines ke beech bina insaan ke loop production mein sabse mushkil se pakde jaane wale bugs mein se hai.
real_world_analogy: Do answering machines ek doosre ko call karke 'please message chhodiye' bolti rahein -- raat bhar.
how_it_works: packet -> decodeHeader -> qr == 1 -> dropped++ -> return undefined -> listen() ka handler kuch nahi bhejta.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handle (header.qr check), ServerStats.dropped; src/transport.ts matchesQuery (resolver side QR rule). Test server.test.ts 'a packet with QR=1 (a response) is dropped, so two servers can never ping-pong'.
advantages: Ek line ka check, poori class of loops khatam
Counter se dikhta hai kitne aise packets aaye
disadvantages: Drop silent hai -- debug karte waqt sirf stats() se pata chalta hai
Test ek negative wait (300 ms) par depend karta hai
common_mistakes: Sirf FORMERR bhejna (woh bhi ek response hai jo loop chala sakta hai)
Resolver aur server dono taraf QR rule na lagana
follow_up_questions: Malformed packets par FORMERR bhejna bhi kya loop bana sakta hai?
dropped counter ko production mein kaise expose karoge?

question: How is the system split between stub server, resolver and transport, and how would you evolve it into a resolver serving a whole office network?
answer_hinglish:
Teen layers hain. src/server.ts ka DnsServer stub clients (nslookup, OS resolver) ke liye front door hai: UDP aur TCP ek hi port par, input validation, rcodes, TC, aur bind guard. Woh khud kuch resolve nahi karta -- Resolver.resolve(name, type) bulata hai. src/resolver.ts iterative resolution karta hai (root -> TLD -> zone, CNAME chain, bailiwick, limits) aur cache rakhta hai. src/transport.ts sirf 'ek query, ek server' jaanta hai: UDP spoofing checks, TCP framing. Wire format sab ke neeche src/wire.ts mein. Client ka RD=1 query server leta hai; upstream sab RD=0 jaata hai (mutation R10 isko pakadta hai); reply mein RA=1.

Yeh split testability deta hai: resolver ka 'route' hook fake network par point karta hai, server tests real sockets par fake network ke through chalte hain, transport ki checks fakenet ke spoof() hook se.

Office network ke liye (ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK private LAN par) jo cheezein abhi NAHI hain aur chahiye: (1) access control -- client subnet allowlist, warna open resolver; (2) rate limiting per client; (3) max concurrent resolutions, kyunki abhi har UDP packet ek async handle() shuru karta hai bina limit ke; (4) in-flight dedupe -- 50 laptops ek saath same naam poochein toh 50 upstream walks; (5) RTT-based server selection aur dead-server memory; (6) EDNS(0) taaki kam TCP; (7) metrics -- stats() counters ko export karna; (8) multiple processes ke liye shared cache ya per-process cache ka acceptance. README ki NOT implemented list mein yeh sab likha hai.
why_needed: Senior interview mein yeh dekhte hain ki aap apne learning project ki seemaayein jaante ho aur production ka raasta bata sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Hotel: reception (server) guest ki request leta hai, concierge (resolver) bahar jaakar info laata hai, aur courier (transport) sirf ek jagah se ek cheez laata hai.
how_it_works: client --RD=1--> DnsServer.handle -> Resolver.resolve -> (cache | askZone -> exchange -> queryUdp/queryTcp --RD=0--> authoritative) -> Resolution -> base() + answers -> TC check -> client.
in_this_project: src/server.ts DnsServer (listen, onTcp, handle), src/resolver.ts Resolver (resolve, exchange, route option), src/transport.ts queryUdp/queryTcp. src/index.ts sab ko jodta hai. Tests: test/server.test.ts server ko real Resolver aur fake network ke saath chalata hai.
advantages: Har layer alag test hoti hai
Server ko resolver ke internals nahi pata
route hook se poora network fake ho sakta hai
disadvantages: Ek process, ek cache -- horizontal scaling ka koi design nahi
Server mein concurrency limit nahi
common_mistakes: Server ke andar resolution logic daal dena
Upstream ko bhi RD=1 bhejna
Stub server ko 'internal' maan kar ACL skip karna
follow_up_questions: In-flight dedupe kis layer mein jaayega?
Multiple instances ke beech cache share karoge ya nahi?
Forwarder mode (upstream resolver ko RD=1) kaise add karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Clean layers testability dete hain, par cross-cutting cheezein (rate limit, dedupe, metrics) ke liye jagah tay karni padti hai: rate limit server mein, dedupe resolver mein (resolve() ke aage ek Map of promises), RTT stats transport/resolver ke beech.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Office mein ek slow ya dead authoritative server har us lookup ko timeoutMs tak rokta hai jo usse pehle chune; bina concurrency limit ke query burst memory aur sockets kha sakta hai; process crash par poora cache jaata hai.
advanced.alternatives: Unbound/BIND jaisa mature resolver; ya forwarder setup (stub server -> trusted upstream). Learning ke liye hand-written, production ke liye proven software typically.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x clients par in-flight dedupe aur cache hit rate sabse bade levers hain; 100x par multiple instances, anycast ya load balancer, aur per-instance cache (DNS caches typically share-nothing chalte hain).
advanced.production_improvements: Subnet ACL, per-client token bucket, semaphore on handle(), dedupe map, RTT-sorted servers, EDNS(0), Prometheus-style counters stats() se, serve-stale.

question: How does the stub server handle several pipelined queries on one TCP connection, and why can the replies come back out of order?
answer_hinglish:
RFC 7766 kehta hai ki DNS over TCP par client ek connection par kai queries bhej sakta hai (pipelining) aur server unhe parallel process karke kisi bhi order mein jawab de sakta hai -- client har reply ko ID se match karta hai.

DnsServer.onTcp mein har connection ka apna LengthPrefixedReader hai. 'data' event par reader.feed(chunk) jitne poore frames de, un sab ke liye 'void this.handle(frame, "tcp").then(out => s.write(frameTcp(out)))' -- matlab har frame ka handle() ek alag promise hai, koi await ek doosre ka nahi. Agar query 1 ko root se teen hops lagne hain aur query 2 cache se turant aa jaaye, toh query 2 ka reply pehle likha jaayega. Yeh allowed hai, aur isiliye test 'TCP: several pipelined queries on one connection, the last split across writes' replies ke IDs ko SORT karke [1, 2] se compare karta hai, order assume nahi karta.

Node single-threaded hai, toh s.write calls interleave nahi hote -- har frameTcp(out) ek hi write mein poora jaata hai, toh frames aapas mein mix nahi hote. '!s.destroyed' check zaroori hai: client ne beech mein connection band kar diya ya idle timeout (tcpIdleMs, default 10000 ms) ne destroy kiya, toh baad mein khatam hone wala resolve band socket par likhne ki koshish na kare.

Kya nahi hai: per-connection ya global concurrency limit. Ek client ek connection par bahut saari queries pipeline karke bahut saare parallel resolutions chala sakta hai -- yeh rate limiting wali NOT implemented list mein aata hai.
why_needed: TCP pipelining ke bina har TCP query ek naya handshake maangti; aur ordering assume karne wala client ya test galat hoga.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein ek table ne teen dishes order ki: jo pehle bane woh pehle aati hai, waiter order number dekh kar rakhta hai -- order kram se nahi.
how_it_works: data -> reader.feed -> [f1, f2] -> handle(f1) aur handle(f2) dono shuru -> jo pehle resolve ho -> write(frameTcp(reply)) (agar socket zinda hai).
in_this_project: src/server.ts onTcp (sockets Set, setTimeout tcpIdleMs, LengthPrefixedReader, !s.destroyed), close() saare sockets destroy karta hai. Test server.test.ts tcpExchange helper: saare frames ek write mein, last ke 3 bytes 20 ms baad.
advantages: Slow query fast query ko block nahi karti (no head-of-line blocking at app level)
Ek connection, kai queries
Idle connections apne aap band
disadvantages: Concurrency limit nahi
Socket error silently ignore hota hai (s.on('error', () => {}))

pehle handle() reject hota toh unhandled rejection ban sakta tha; yeh gap interview bank likhte waqt mila aur fix hua (resolver ka exception -> SERVFAIL, socket callback mein rejection -> dropped counter)
common_mistakes: Replies ko request order mein maan lena
Band socket par write karna
Ek TCP connection par sirf ek query support karna
follow_up_questions: Per-connection in-flight limit kaise lagaoge?
Client side queryTcp pipelining kyun nahi karta?
Idle timeout ka sahi value kaise chunoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har frame ka parallel handle() latency ke liye best hai par backpressure nahi deta. Sequential processing (ek ke baad ek) safe hota par ek slow lookup baaki sab ko rokta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Client 1000 queries pipeline kare: 1000 parallel resolutions, har ek ke upstream sockets -- file descriptors aur memory. Client band kare: !s.destroyed se write skip hota hai, par resolution phir bhi poori chalti hai (cancel nahi hoti).
advanced.alternatives: Per-connection semaphore (max N in-flight), ya s.pause() jab in-flight zyada ho; AbortSignal se resolution cancel karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare TCP clients par sockets Set aur idle timeouts memory decide karte hain; production servers typically max TCP clients ki limit rakhte hain.
advanced.production_improvements: In-flight counter per socket aur global, limit par s.pause()/resume(); rejected replies ko sirf gin-na nahi balki log bhi karna; idle timeout config se.

question: Why does every upstream UDP query get its own socket, and what does that mean for many concurrent lookups?
answer_hinglish:
Do design ho sakte hain. Shared socket: ek UDP socket sab queries ke liye, aur ek demux table (ID -> pending promise). Ya per-query socket: har query ka apna socket, apna random port, apna listener. Yeh project doosra chunta hai, aur reason security hai.

Shared socket matlab fixed source port -- spoofing entropy sirf 16-bit ID tak gir jaati hai (mutation T4 yahi hai). Per-query socket par har query ka port random hai, aur demux table ki zaroorat hi nahi: socket par aaya har packet sirf usi query ka candidate hai, aur queryUdp ka handler usse source + matchesQuery se check karta hai. Concurrency simple ho jaati hai -- koi shared mutable map nahi, koi race nahi ki do in-flight queries ka same ID ho jaaye.

Cost: har query ek socket create, bind (kabhi retry), aur close. Bahut saari concurrent lookups ka matlab utne hi open sockets -- file descriptor limit aur bind collisions (bindRandom 8 attempts deta hai). Resolver ke andar ek resolution sequential hai (askZone servers ek ke baad ek try karta hai), toh ek resolve() ek waqt par ek hi upstream socket kholta hai; concurrency server ke parallel handle() calls se aati hai.

Kya nahi hai: in-flight deduplication. README: 'two identical concurrent queries both go upstream.' Do clients ek saath www.alpha.test poochein toh do poori walks -- do sockets, aur cache poisoning ke liye attacker ko do races ka mauka. Production resolvers same (name, type) ke in-flight queries ko ek promise par jodte hain.
why_needed: Socket design security (entropy), simplicity (demux) aur resources (FDs) teeno ko ek saath affect karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Har courier ke liye alag, random number wala PO box: koi andaza nahi laga sakta ki aapka parcel kis box mein aayega, aur box par aaya har parcel bas ek order ka hai.
how_it_works: resolve -> askZone -> exchange -> queryUdp: bindRandom -> send -> listen -> finish -> sock.close(). N parallel handle() -> N parallel resolutions -> har ek ka ek active socket.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts queryUdp aur bindRandom (finish() mein sock.close()), src/resolver.ts askZone (sequential loop) aur exchange. README NOT implemented: 'No in-flight deduplication'.
advantages: Har query random port
Koi shared demux state nahi
Ek query ka garbage doosri ko affect nahi karta
disadvantages: Per query syscall overhead
FD usage concurrency ke saath linear
In-flight dedupe nahi
common_mistakes: Shared socket aur sequential IDs
Socket close bhoolna (timeout path par bhi finish() close karta hai)
Dedupe key mein naam ka case normalise na karna
follow_up_questions: Dedupe se poisoning risk kaise kam hota hai?
FD limit hit ho toh kya error aayega aur resolver kya karega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Per-query socket security aur simplicity khareedta hai, resources ki keemat par. Shared socket + demux sasta hai par port entropy chali jaati hai -- jab tak ek pool of random-port sockets na ho.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Burst mein FD exhaustion -> bindRandom fail -> TransportError -> askZone next server -> sab fail -> SERVFAIL. Dedupe na hone se same naam ke liye multiple races.
advanced.alternatives: Random ports ka socket pool (har socket kuch queries, ID se demux); ya OS-level port randomisation par bharosa (platform dependent).

question: Where does this resolver spend time and resources on the transport side, and what would you change first to make it faster?
answer_hinglish:
Seedhi baat: README koi timing claim nahi karta ('a handful of manual runs is not a measurement'), toh main numbers nahi, cost centres bataunga.

1. Network round trips -- sabse bada. Cold lookup root -> TLD -> zone, har hop ek RTT. Cache ke baad sibling names seedha zone cut se (test 'a sibling name starts at the cached zone cut' -- 1 query).
2. Timeouts. Dead server poora timeoutMs (default 2000) khaata hai, aur servers har baar random order mein try hote hain -- koi RTT memory nahi. Yeh tail latency ka sabse bada source hai.
3. TC -> TCP. Hum EDNS(0) nahi bhejte, toh 512 bytes se bada har upstream answer pehle UDP par truncated aata hai, phir TCP connect + handshake + poora answer -- ek extra RTT plus handshake. Stub server bhi client ke liye 512 par cap karta hai.
4. Per-query socket: create + bind + close har UDP query par.
5. Encode/decode: chhote messages, typically network ke saamne negligible.

Pehle kya badlunga (impact ke order mein): (a) RTT-based server selection aur dead/lame server memory -- timeouts kam; (b) in-flight dedupe; (c) EDNS(0) with a sensible UDP buffer size, taaki kam TCP fallback; (d) prefetch/serve-stale taaki popular names kabhi cold na hon. Socket pooling tabhi jab profiling dikhaye. Sab README ki NOT implemented list mein hain -- matlab design inke liye jagah chhodta hai: Resolver ke options (timeoutMs, shuffle) aur onIgnored/trace hooks measurement ke liye ready hain.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhta hai ki aap bina data ke numbers nahi banate aur sahi bottleneck pehchante ho.
real_world_analogy: Delivery boy ka time zyada traffic (RTT) aur band dukaan par khade rehne (timeout) mein jaata hai, bike start karne (socket) mein nahi.
how_it_works: latency = sum(RTT per hop) + timeouts on dead servers + TC fallback (TCP handshake + RTT) + small CPU. Cache hits hops hataate hain.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts askZone (shuffled order, timeouts), exchange (TC -> queryTcp), Resolver options timeoutMs/shuffle; src/transport.ts queryUdp per-query socket; src/server.ts UDP_MAX_ANSWER. CLI 'resolve' trace har hop dikhata hai aur total ms print karta hai.
advantages: Cost centres saaf alag hain aur trace mein dikhte hain
Cache zone cuts ko reuse karta hai
disadvantages: Koi RTT memory nahi
No EDNS -> zyada TCP
Koi benchmark nahi hai
common_mistakes: Bina measurement ke socket pooling jaise micro-optimisations pehle karna
Timeout bahut chhota karke legit slow servers ko dead bana dena
Performance numbers invent karna
follow_up_questions: RTT estimate ke liye kaunsa algorithm (smoothed RTT jaisa) use karoge?
EDNS buffer size kya rakhoge aur kyun?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Random server order load phailata hai aur simple hai, par RTT-based selection latency kam karta hai -- production resolvers typically RTT ke saath thoda randomness rakhte hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek root/TLD server unreachable ho aur bar bar pehle chuna jaaye: har cold lookup par 2 s extra. TCP fallback ke time upstream TCP block ho toh truncated answers SERVFAIL ban jaate hain.
advanced.alternatives: Forwarding to a big public resolver (unki cache hits), ya local cache ko bada aur long-lived rakhna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par dedupe aur cache hit rate; 100x par multi-instance, aur upstream servers ki taraf se rate limits ka dhyaan.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-server SRTT + backoff, dedupe, EDNS(0), prefetch, histogram metrics per hop -- pehle measure, phir optimise.

question: How does the stub server's reply map onto the resolver's data model of RRsets and negative entries, and why is there no cache of whole responses?
answer_hinglish:
Cache ek chhota data store hai, aur uska schema RRset-level hai, response-level nahi. Positive entries key (name, type) par poora RRset rakhti hain, TTL set ka minimum aur read par count down; negative entries NXDOMAIN ke liye sirf NAME par (saare types), NODATA ke liye name + type par, SOA ke saath. Rank batata hai data answer se aaya ya referral (NS, glue) se.

Stub server is model ko seedha use karta hai. DnsServer.handle resolver.resolve(q.name, q.type) bulata hai aur Resolution milta hai: answers (CNAME chain kram mein, phir final RRset), authority (negative ke liye SOA), rcode. Server sirf in dono ko reply.answers aur reply.authority mein daalta hai, additional khaali. Cache ka har read TTL ko count down karta hai, toh client ko remaining TTL milta hai.

Whole-response cache kyun nahi? README ki NOT implemented list mein 'no cache of whole responses' hai. RRset model ka fayda: ek hi RRset kai responses mein reuse hota hai -- www.alpha.test A direct query mein bhi, aur alias.alpha.test ki CNAME chain ke end mein bhi. Har RRset apna TTL rakhta hai, toh chain ka har link apne time par expire hota hai. Response cache har baar response banane ka CPU bachata, par stale TTLs, duplicate storage aur invalidation ka jhanjhat laata. Production servers kabhi dono rakhte hain: RRset cache as source of truth, upar ek message cache.
why_needed: Interview mein 'cache key kya hai, kya store karte ho' ek database schema sawaal hi hai.
real_world_analogy: Library mein kitaabein (RRsets) shelf par rakhte ho, har student ke liye photocopy ka bundle (response) nahi -- bundle har baar kitaabon se banta hai.
how_it_works: query (name,type) -> Resolver: cache.getNegative / getRRset ya upstream -> Resolution{rcode, answers[], authority[]} -> server base(rcode,[q]) + answers + authority -> encode.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Cache (putRRset, getRRset, putNegative, getNegative, Rank). src/resolver.ts Resolution interface. src/server.ts handle mein reply.answers = res.answers; reply.authority = res.authority. Test server.test.ts 'NXDOMAIN with the SOA in authority; a CNAME chain in the answer'.
advantages: RRset reuse across responses
Har RRset ka apna TTL
Negative entries RFC 2308 ke hisaab se
disadvantages: Har query par response dobara encode
Eviction insertion-order hai, LRU nahi
Process restart par cache khatam
common_mistakes: Response ko (name,type) par cache karke andar ke TTLs freeze kar dena
Referral glue ko answer ki tarah client ko dena
NXDOMAIN ko per type cache karna
follow_up_questions: Message cache add karoge toh TTL kaise sahi rakhoge?
Cache ko Redis mein le jaana sahi rahega?

question: nslookup example.com 127.0.0.1 -port=5300 times out against the running stub server. How did you find the cause and what is the fix?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: server 127.0.0.1:5300 par chal raha hai (listening log line aayi), lekin Windows nslookup -port=5300 ke saath timeout deta hai.

Investigation: pehle server side -- kya packet aaya bhi? TRACE=1 ya stats() ke udpQueries counter se dikhta hai ki koi query aayi hi nahi. Toh problem client side hai. Phir test: do plain UDP listeners lagaye, ek port 53 par aur ek N par, aur nslookup -port=N chalaya (set port=N bhi try kiya). Sirf 53 wale listener par packets aaye, N par kabhi nahi.

Cause: is Windows 11 build (10.0.26200) ka nslookup.exe -port aur set port ko IGNORE karta hai aur hamesha 53 par bhejta hai. PLAN.md ka original idea ('nslookup example.com 127.0.0.1 -port=N') isi wajah se badalna pada.

Fix: nslookup ke liye server ko PORT=53 par chalao (PowerShell: $env:PORT=53; npm start). Loopback par 53 bind karne ke liye is machine par admin rights nahi lage. dig jahan ho wahan 'dig -p' kaam karta hai (yahan installed nahi tha). CLI listen ke baad yahi hint print karta hai: '(Windows nslookup ignores -port; run with PORT=53 for it)'.

Test design par asar: always-on interop test nslookup.exe ke CAPTURED packets use karta hai (PTR for 1.0.0.127.in-addr.arpa, phir A, phir AAAA, sab RD=1, no EDNS), aur live nslookup run opt-in (INTEROP_NSLOOKUP=1) hai kyunki use 127.0.0.1:53 bind karna padta hai jo doosri machines par local DNS service se clash kar sakta hai.
why_needed: Tool ka documented flag kaam na kare toh ghante barbaad hote hain; pehle 'packet aaya ya nahi' prove karna sabse fast raasta hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko flat number 5300 bola par woh hamesha building ke main gate (53) par hi parcel chhod deta hai -- flat ke bahar wait karte raho, kuch nahi aayega.
how_it_works: server counters/trace -> zero queries -> client side suspect -> listeners on 53 and N -> only 53 receives -> nslookup ignores -port -> run server on 53.
in_this_project: test/interop.test.ts header comment aur NSLOOKUP_PACKETS (captured hex), RecordingServer jo har packet decode karke seen mein rakhta hai. src/index.ts ki 'try:' hint line. README 'Interop with real tools' aur PLAN.md 'Decisions changed'.
code_example:
# PowerShell, as in README
$env:PORT=53; npm start
nslookup example.com. 127.0.0.1
nslookup -type=MX gmail.com. 127.0.0.1
# opt-in live interop test (binds 127.0.0.1:53)
$env:INTEROP_NSLOOKUP=1; npm test

Captured packets se test bina nslookup ke bhi chalta hai
disadvantages: Port 53 kisi aur DNS service se clash kar sakta hai
Finding ek specific Windows build par hai; doosre builds alag ho sakte hain
common_mistakes: Server ko blame karna bina check kiye ki packet aaya
Ek hi listener se conclusion nikaalna
Live tool par depend test ko default on rakhna

Linux par yahi test kaise karoge?

question: How do the mutation checks T1-T5 and S1-S6 prove the transport and server defences are actually tested, and what would you do if one survived?
answer_hinglish:
Line coverage sirf yeh batata hai ki code chala; yeh nahi ki koi test usse fail hota agar code galat ho. Mutation check mein ek rule ko jaan-boojh kar todte hain (src mein ek exact text replacement), poora suite chalate hain, aur file restore karte hain. Kam se kam ek test red hua toh check 'caught'.

Transport: T1 reply ID check hataya -> 1 test fail ('a reply with the wrong ID is ignored'); T2 source address/port check hataya -> 1 ('a reply from a different source port...', fakenet ka spoof() hook doosre port se bhejta hai); T3 question check -> 1; T4 fixed source port -> 1 aur T5 fixed ID -> 1, dono 'query IDs and source ports are random' se. Server: S1 non-loopback bind -> 1 (bind guard test); S2 big UDP answers not truncated -> 2; S3 QR=1 answered -> 1; S4 malformed dropped instead of FORMERR -> 1; S5 reply ID copy nahi -> 4; S6 ANY/AXFR resolver ko -> 1. Saare 11 caught.

Survive hone par kya? Is project mein 41 mein se 5 pehli baar nahi pakde gaye. Process: (1) samjho test kyun pass hua -- W3 mein error ek LATER check se aa raha tha, R8/R9 mein ek hi test do limits se rukta tha; (2) aisa test likho jo SIRF us rule ko pin kare (readName seedha [0, 0xc0] par, maxQueries: 2, maxDepth: 0); (3) mutation dobara chalao aur dekho naya test hi pakadta hai. Agar mutant equivalent ho (W4 -- behaviour badalta hi nahi), toh likh do aur kyun check rakha.

Notice karo T-checks mein zyaadatar ek hi test pakadta hai -- matlab woh test critical hai; use flaky ya skip karna defence ko untested chhod dega.
why_needed: Security checks ka 'test hai' kehna kaafi nahi; mutation dikhata hai ki test sach mein us check par depend karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire alarm test: dhuan jaan-boojh kar chhodo aur dekho alarm baja ya nahi. Sirf 'alarm laga hua hai' dekhna kaafi nahi.
how_it_works: for each rule: apply one text replacement -> npm test -> count failures -> restore -> git status clean. 0 failures -> analyse -> targeted test -> re-run.
in_this_project: README 'Mutation checks (2026-11-21)' table (T1-T5, S1-S6 aur baaki). Tests: test/resolver.test.ts spoofing block, test/server.test.ts. test/fakenet.ts ka spoof hook T2 ke liye zaroori hai.
advantages: Har defence ke peeche ek red test proven hai
Gaps (W3, W7, R8, R9) ko targeted tests se band kiya
Equivalent mutant honestly documented
disadvantages: Manual process, CI mein automated nahi
Ek mutation per rule -- har possible bug nahi
common_mistakes: Coverage % ko test quality samajhna
Mutation ke baad file restore na karna
Survived mutant par check hi hata dena
follow_up_questions: Stryker jaisa tool use karoge toh kya badlega?
Equivalent mutant kaise pehchante ho?
T2 ke liye spoof hook kaise kaam karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hand-picked mutations sasti aur focused hain (har ek ek documented rule), par automated mutation testing har operator ko todti hai aur zyada gaps dhoondhti -- bahut zyada noise aur time ke saath.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi critical test (jaise 'query IDs and source ports are random') flaky ho kar skip ho gaya, toh T4 aur T5 dono untested ho jaate. Randomness wala test '>= 18 of 20' threshold se flakiness kam rakhta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Stryker Mutator (TypeScript), property-based tests, ya fuzzing (wire format ke liye 6000 packets pehle se hain).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Code badhe toh har naye rule ke saath ek naya mutation row; 10x code par automated tool hi practical hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Mutation script ko repo mein rakhna (replacement + expected failing test), CI mein weekly run, survived mutants par build fail.

question: You want to use this resolver for real lookups on a Windows laptop with nslookup. Walk through the setup and what you would check at each step.
answer_hinglish:
Step 1: build aur chalaao. npm install, npm run build. Pehle ek one-off check: 'node dist/index.js resolve www.wikipedia.org A' -- trace har hop dikhata hai (root -> org -> wikipedia.org, CNAME dyna.wikimedia.org, aur dusri baar org NS cache se). Last line mein rcode aur upstream queries ki ginti. Agar yahin timeout aaye toh outbound UDP/TCP 53 blocked hai (firewall, corporate network) -- server chalane ka fayda nahi.

Step 2: server port 53 par, kyunki is Windows build ka nslookup -port ignore karta hai. PowerShell: $env:PORT=53; npm start. Listening JSON line mein host 127.0.0.1 aur port 53 dikhna chahiye. HOST default 127.0.0.1 hai; ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK set mat karo. Port 53 already busy ho (local DNS service) toh bind fail hoga.

Step 3: query karo -- nslookup example.com. 127.0.0.1 aur nslookup -type=MX gmail.com. 127.0.0.1. Trailing dot important hai, warna nslookup apne search suffixes jod sakta hai. Note karo nslookup pehle 1.0.0.127.in-addr.arpa ka PTR poochta hai (server ka naam dikhane ke liye) -- real internet par us ka jawab jo bhi aaye, main query phir bhi chalti hai.

Step 4: debugging ke liye TRACE=1 se har upstream query print hoti hai; Ctrl+C par 'stopping' line mein stats() ke counters (udpQueries, tcpQueries, formerr, notimp, servfail, truncated, dropped).

Step 5: bada answer test karna ho toh nslookup -vc (TCP). README ke hisaab se example.com aur gmail.com MX dono is machine par real root servers se resolve hue. Isko OS ka system DNS banana NOT recommended -- koi serve-stale, RTT selection ya hardening nahi hai.
why_needed: Real tool ke saath end-to-end chalana dikhata hai ki aapka server standard clients ke saath sach mein interoperate karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Naye ghar mein bijli check: pehle main switch (outbound 53), phir meter (server bind), phir ek bulb (nslookup) -- har step ka alag test.
how_it_works: resolve CLI (connectivity) -> PORT=53 serve (bind) -> nslookup with trailing dot (UDP) -> -vc (TCP) -> TRACE / stats for evidence.
in_this_project: src/index.ts (resolve mode, PORT/HOST/TRACE env, listening/stopping logs), src/server.ts stats(). README 'Run it' aur 'Interop with real tools'. Captured nslookup packets test/interop.test.ts mein.

npm install
npm run build
node dist/index.js resolve www.wikipedia.org A     # every step printed
$env:PORT=53; $env:TRACE=1; npm start              # PowerShell
nslookup example.com. 127.0.0.1
