question: Your team wants to run the stub server on a shared lab network with ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1. What risks do you raise and what would you build before agreeing?
answer_hinglish:
Main seedha kahunga: abhi ke code ke saath yeh sirf ek trusted, firewalled lab network par, aur woh bhi temporary. Reason: ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1 ke baad yeh ek recursive resolver hai jismein README ke hisaab se 'no rate limiting, no access control beyond the loopback guard, no max concurrent queries'.

Risks: (1) Amplification -- agar network ka koi raasta internet se aata hai, ya lab ke andar koi spoofed source bhej sake, toh hum kisi victim ki taraf traffic badha sakte hain. ANY/AXFR NOTIMP hain, jo madad karta hai, par bade TXT answers bhi kaam karte hain. (2) Resource exhaustion -- har UDP packet ek async handle() shuru karta hai, har resolution upstream sockets kholta hai; flood memory aur FDs kha sakta hai. (3) Cache poisoning ka shared impact -- ab ek poisoned entry sab users ko lagti hai; DNSSEC nahi hai. (4) Crash risk -- interview bank likhte waqt mila ki resolver ka unexpected (non-ResolveError) exception unhandled rejection ban ke process gira sakta tha; ab handle() use SERVFAIL bana deta hai (test: "an unexpected exception from the resolver becomes SERVFAIL, not a crash") aur socket callbacks ka rejection sirf dropped counter badhata hai. Phir bhi ek process sab clients ka single point of failure hai.

Agree karne se pehle main banaunga: client subnet allowlist (listen ke baad handle mein rinfo.address check, REFUSED ya drop); per-client token bucket rate limit; global in-flight semaphore; rejected replies ki logging (abhi sirf dropped counter); stats() counters ka metrics endpoint aur alerts (formerr, dropped, servfail spikes); in-flight dedupe; process supervisor (restart). Aur kabhi public interface par bind nahi -- index.ts ka message bhi yahi kehta hai. Lambi avadhi ke liye: mature resolver use karo, ya isko forwarder ki tarah ek hardened resolver ke peeche rakho.
why_needed: Senior role mein 'haan, flag set kar do' nahi, risk aur conditions batana expected hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka Wi-Fi password poore mohalle ko dena: chalega, par pehle guest network, speed limit aur router ka log chahiye.
how_it_works: Today: any client -> handle -> resolve, no limits. Target: rinfo -> ACL -> rate limiter -> semaphore -> handle (with catch) -> metrics.
in_this_project: src/server.ts listen (allowNonLoopback), handle (no ACL), udp.on('message') handler; src/index.ts ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK warning. README 'NOT implemented yet' Stub server line.
advantages: Risk ka saaf, testable list
Har mitigation existing hooks (rinfo, stats) par ban sakta hai
disadvantages: Kaafi kaam chahiye jo abhi nahi hai
Ek process -- single point of failure
common_mistakes: Firewall ko akela control maan lena
Rate limit ke bina ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK
Crash ko 'rare' maan kar supervisor na rakhna
follow_up_questions: REFUSED bhejoge ya drop karoge? Kyun?
Rate limiter ka key client IP hai -- spoofed source mein kya problem hai?
Kitne samay mein cache poisoning detect karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har mitigation latency ya complexity jodta hai; ACL sabse sasta aur sabse zyada value deta hai, rate limiting ko spoofed sources ke saath sochna padta hai (UDP par limit ka key forge ho sakta hai -- RRL isliye responses ko limit karta hai).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flood -> sockets/memory -> SERVFAIL sab ke liye; unexpected exception -> process down; poisoned entry -> sab users galat IP par; upstream servers hamara IP rate-limit kar dein.
advanced.alternatives: Unbound ya BIND as the lab resolver; ya stub server ko sirf ek trusted forwarder ke saath; ya har developer apne laptop par loopback par chalaaye (aaj ka safe default).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x users par dedupe aur cache hit rate; 100x par multiple instances aur ek LB, per-instance limits, aur centralised metrics.
advanced.production_improvements: Subnet ACL, RRL-style rate limiting, semaphore, catch + SERVFAIL, metrics + alerts, supervisor, DNSSEC roadmap, aur regular mutation checks naye guards ke liye.

question: What failure modes does queryTcp handle, and how do they turn into trying the next server instead of a failed lookup?
answer_hinglish:
queryTcp mein ek single finish() function hai jo 'done' flag se sirf ek baar chalta hai: timer clear, sock.destroy(), aur resolve ya reject. Har failure isi se guzarta hai, toh double-resolve ya socket leak nahi hota. Cases:

1. Connect fail (connection refused, unreachable) -> 'error' event -> TransportError.
2. Server connection band kar de reply se pehle -> 'close' event -> TransportError('TCP connection ... closed before a reply'). Note: successful finish ke baad bhi destroy 'close' fire karta hai, par done flag use ignore kar deta hai.
3. Kuch aaya hi nahi -> timer -> TimeoutError('no TCP reply ...').
4. Frame decode nahi hua -> WireError (as is) ya TransportError.
5. Frame decode hua par matchesQuery fail -> TransportError('TCP reply does not match the query'). UDP ke ulat, yahan ignore nahi -- TCP par off-path injection practical nahi, toh mismatch matlab broken server.
6. Adhura frame aur connection band -> case 2.

Resolver.exchange TC par queryTcp ko ek NAYE randomId ke saath bulata hai. Jo bhi error aaye, askZone use catch karta hai (TimeoutError, TransportError, WireError), trace mein likhta hai, failures list mein jodta hai aur zone ka next server try karta hai. Sab servers fail toh ResolveError('all servers for zone ... failed') -> resolve() SERVFAIL deta hai reason ke saath. Matlab ek server ka TCP toota ho toh lookup bachta hai, bas thoda late.

Ek honest gap: TCP par timeout poora timeoutMs hai, UDP wale ke upar -- TC ke baad ek bura server do timeouts le sakta hai. Aur client side TCP pipelining ya connection reuse nahi; har TC retry naya connection.
why_needed: TCP fallback rare path hai; rare paths mein hi aksar socket leaks aur double-callback bugs chhupte hain.
real_world_analogy: Phone call: number nahi laga (error), utha ke kaat diya (close), koi utha hi nahi (timeout), galat aadmi ne utha liya (mismatch) -- har case mein agla number try karo.
how_it_works: connect -> write(frameTcp) -> data -> reader.feed -> decode -> matchesQuery -> finish(ok). error/close/timer/decode/mismatch -> finish(err) -> askZone catch -> next server.
in_this_project: src/transport.ts queryTcp (finish with done flag, timer, error/close/data handlers), TimeoutError, TransportError. src/resolver.ts exchange (TC -> queryTcp with new ID), askZone (catch and continue). Test resolver.test.ts 'a truncated (TC) UDP reply is retried over TCP to the same server'.
advantages: Ek finish(), ek exit path -- leak aur double resolve nahi
Har failure typed error, resolver ek jagah handle karta hai
disadvantages: TC ke baad worst case do timeouts
Har retry naya TCP connection
common_mistakes: 'close' handler ko success ke baad bhi error maan lena (done flag ke bina)
Timer clear na karna
TCP mismatch ko ignore karke wait karna
follow_up_questions: TCP failure par UDP answer (truncated) use karna kabhi theek hai?
Connection reuse (RFC 7766) kaise add karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fail-fast TCP aur next server simple aur robust hai; same server par TCP dobara try karna kabhi transient errors bachata, par latency badhata.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Network jahan outbound TCP 53 blocked ho: har bada answer SERVFAIL. Server jo TCP accept karke kabhi jawab na de: poora timeoutMs per server.
advanced.alternatives: EDNS(0) se kam TCP; TCP connection pool per server; overall per-resolution deadline taaki do timeouts add na hon.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut TCP traffic par connection setup cost dikhega; production resolvers typically connections reuse karte hain aur idle timeout rakhte hain.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-resolution deadline, TCP failure metrics per server, EDNS(0), aur jo server TCP mein fail ho use kuch der neeche rakhna.

question: What is 0x20 case randomisation, why isn't it in this resolver, and how would you add it without breaking the existing tests?
answer_hinglish:
0x20 (draft by Dagon et al., widely deployed) ek trick hai jo spoofing ke liye extra entropy deta hai bina protocol badle. Query ke naam ke har letter ka case random karo -- wWw.aLpHa.TeSt. Authoritative servers question ko byte-for-byte echo karte hain, toh genuine reply mein wahi case aata hai. Attacker ko ID aur port ke saath har letter ka case bhi guess karna padega: har alphabetic character ek extra bit. Lambe naamon par yeh kaafi bits hain; numbers aur chhote naamon par kam.

Is project mein implement nahi hai -- README do baar kehta hai: 'Also not done: 0x20 case randomisation, which would add more bits.' Reason design mein hai: matchesQuery naam ko sameName se compare karta hai, jo canonicalName par based case-INSENSITIVE hai. 0x20 ke liye exact-case compare chahiye.

Add karne ka plan: (1) Resolver.exchange mein buildQuery se pehle naam ko randomise karo (crypto.randomInt se per-letter bit), aur original naam yaad rakho. (2) transport mein ek option, jaise strictCase, jisse matchesQuery r.name === q.name bhi maange. (3) Cache aur classify ke liye original (canonical) naam use karo, taaki bailiwick aur cache keys na badlein. (4) Fallback: kuch servers case echo nahi karte; aise server ke liye mismatch par same server ko bina 0x20 ke ek baar retry, aur server ko yaad rakhna -- yeh production resolvers ka common pattern hai. (5) Tests: fakenet question echo karta hai, toh existing tests chalenge; naya test -- ek hook jo case badal kar echo kare, aur expect karo 'mismatch' ignored. Phir mutation: strict compare hatao, test red hona chahiye.

Ek subtle point: wire.ts case-insensitive compression karta hai -- humare outgoing query mein sirf ek naam hai, toh problem nahi, par yeh dhyan dene wali jagah hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap existing defences ke upar sasta incremental hardening soch sakte ho aur uske compatibility costs jaante ho.
real_world_analogy: Signature ke saath har baar alag rang ki syahi: asli bank wahi rang wapas dikhayega, nakli ko rang bhi guess karna padega.
how_it_works: query name -> per-letter random case -> send -> reply question must match EXACT case (plus ID, port) -> internally canonical name use.
in_this_project: Implement nahi hai. Relevant code: src/transport.ts matchesQuery (sameName), src/wire.ts sameName/canonicalName, src/resolver.ts exchange (buildQuery). README 'Why random IDs and ports' aur NOT implemented list.
advantages: Protocol change ke bina extra entropy
Lambe naamon par kaafi bits
Existing checks ke upar layer
disadvantages: Case echo na karne wale servers ke liye fallback chahiye
Numeric/short names par kam bits
On-path attacker ke khilaaf bekaar
common_mistakes: Cache key mein randomised naam use kar lena
Escapes (\. aur \DDD) wale labels ka case bhi badal dena
Fallback ke bina strict mode on karna
follow_up_questions: Kitne bits milte hain 'www.alpha.test' par?
DNS cookies 0x20 se behtar kyun ho sakte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sasta aur protocol-compatible, par ek naya compatibility surface (non-echoing servers) aur fallback logic laata hai -- aur fallback khud attacker trigger kar sakta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Kisi zone ke servers case normalise karein: strict mode mein har reply 'mismatch', har lookup timeout -- isliye per-server fallback memory zaroori.
advanced.alternatives: DNS cookies (RFC 7873), TCP for sensitive zones, DNSSEC (asli fix).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale par per-server 'supports 0x20' state ek naya chhota cache ban jaata hai; usse bhi TTL aur eviction chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Feature flag ke saath rollout, mismatch metrics per server, fallback list, aur ek mutation row (strict compare off -> test red).

question: Write unit tests for LengthPrefixedReader and frameTcp: byte-by-byte feeding, several frames in one chunk, and a frame split inside its length prefix.
answer_hinglish:
Abhi LengthPrefixedReader sirf socket-level tests se cover hai (server.test.ts ka pipelining test aur resolver ka TC test). Ek seedha unit test zyada edge cases sasta aur bina network ke pakadta hai. Teen cases jo maayne rakhte hain:

1. Byte-by-byte: har byte alag feed() call mein. Pehle byte par len bhi nahi padhi ja sakti (buf.length >= 2 fail), toh saare calls khaali array dein jab tak last byte na aaye; phir exactly ek frame. Yeh 'length prefix ke beech split' bhi cover karta hai.
2. Coalesced: do frames ek chunk mein -> ek feed() se do frames, order same.
3. Frame plus aadha agla: feed se ek frame aaye aur pending baaki bytes ki ginti de.

Plus round trip: frameTcp(msg) ka pehla 2 bytes big-endian length hona chahiye, aur reader se wahi msg wapas. Ek test copy-semantics ka bhi: returned frame ko modify karna reader ke internal state ko affect na kare (Buffer.from copy ki wajah se).

Mutation soch: agar koi 'if (this.buf.length < 2 + len) break' ko '< len' kar de, toh byte-by-byte test turant red hoga -- frame 2 bytes jaldi nikal jayega aur kat jayega. Yeh vitest mein likha hai, project ka existing test runner.
why_needed: Framing bugs sirf rare split patterns par dikhte hain; unit test har split ko deterministic bana deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Puzzle ke tukde ek-ek karke dena aur check karna ki tasveer tabhi banti hai jab aakhri tukda aaye.
how_it_works: frameTcp -> bytes -> feed in various chunkings -> expect frames equal to original messages, pending equal to leftover.
in_this_project: Target: src/transport.ts LengthPrefixedReader, frameTcp. Existing related test: test/server.test.ts 'TCP: several pipelined queries on one connection, the last split across writes'. Naya test test/ folder mein, vitest ke saath.
advantages: Network ke bina, fast aur deterministic
Har split position cover
Copy semantics bhi pinned
disadvantages: Socket-level behaviour (backpressure, close) cover nahi hota
common_mistakes: Sirf happy path (ek chunk = ek frame) test karna
pending ko ignore karna
Length little-endian maan kar test likhna
follow_up_questions: Har possible split offset par loop wala test kaise likhoge?
Zero-length frame par kya expect karoge?

question: Add a per-client rate limit to the stub server's UDP path (not implemented today): design it, write it, and say how you would test it.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honesty: README ki NOT implemented list mein 'Stub server: no rate limiting' hai. Yeh exercise dikhata hai ki main ise kaise add karunga.

Design: token bucket per client IP. Har IP ka bucket capacity C tokens se shuru, R tokens/second refill (lazy, last-seen time se). Har UDP query ek token. Token na ho toh drop (reply nahi) aur counter badhao. Drop kyun, REFUSED kyun nahi? Spoofed source ke saath REFUSED bhi victim ki taraf ek packet hai; drop amplification ko zero karta hai. Limit sirf UDP par -- TCP par handshake source prove karta hai, waha per-connection in-flight limit behtar hai.

Kahan lagaun? handle() transport-agnostic hai aur rinfo nahi jaanta, toh check listen() ke udp 'message' handler mein, handle() se pehle. Map unbounded na ho, isliye simple cap: size limit par purani entries hatao (cache.ts jaisa oldest-first). Clock injectable taaki test sleep na kare -- yahi pattern cache tests mein hai.

Test: DnsServer ko chhote capacity (jaise 2) aur refill 0 ke saath banao, ek hi socket se 5 queries bhejo, expect karo 2 replies aur stats().rateLimited 3. Doosre socket se bhi same IP (127.0.0.1) hai, toh woh bhi limited -- yeh limitation note karo. Phir clock aage badha kar ek aur query -> reply. Mutation check: limiter ka condition ulta karo -> test red.

Caveat: key client IP hai, aur UDP par IP forge ho sakta hai -- attacker victim ke IP se bhej kar victim ka quota kha sakta hai. Production RRL isliye responses ko (client subnet, answer) ke hisaab se limit karta hai aur kabhi TC=1 'slip' bhejta hai taaki asli client TCP par aa sake.
why_needed: Bina rate limit ke ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK wala server amplification aur resource flood dono ke liye khula hai.
real_world_analogy: Paani ki tanki jo dheere dheere bharti hai: har glass ek token. Koi ek aadmi baar baar aaye toh tanki khaali, use thoda ruk kar aana padega.
how_it_works: udp message -> limiter.allow(rinfo.address, now) ? handle -> send : stats.rateLimited++ (drop).
in_this_project: Implement nahi hai. Jahan lagega: src/server.ts listen() ka udp.on('message') handler, ServerStats mein naya counter, ServerOptions mein limits. Test pattern: test/server.test.ts udpExchange helper aur stats() test.
advantages: Simple, O(1) per packet
Injectable clock se fast tests
Map size bounded
disadvantages: Spoofed IP se victim ka quota khaya ja sakta hai
Ek NAT ke peeche ke saare users ek bucket share karte
Per-process -- multiple instances mein alag alag
common_mistakes: Limit handle() ke andar lagana jahan client address hi nahi hai
Unbounded Map (khud ek DoS)
Drop ki jagah REFUSED bhejna aur amplification ka ek chhota raasta chhodna
follow_up_questions: RRL ka 'slip' kya hai aur kyun?
Subnet (/24) par key karna IP se behtar kab hai?
TCP ke liye kya limit lagaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Per-IP token bucket simple hai par UDP par key forge ho sakta hai; RRL (response-based) zyada sahi par complex. Drop vs REFUSED vs TC slip: amplification vs legitimate client ka experience.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Attacker victim ke IP se flood -> victim ka DNS band (limiter khud DoS tool). Bahut saare spoofed IPs -> map churn, har packet naya bucket.
advanced.alternatives: RRL (response rate limiting), network-level rate limits (firewall), ya resolver ko sirf allowlisted subnets ke liye kholna (ACL zyada simple aur strong).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x clients par map ka size aur eviction policy maayne rakhti hai; multi-instance par limits per-instance hote hain, global limit ke liye shared store chahiye (latency cost).
advanced.production_improvements: Subnet-based keys, RRL with slip, metrics on rateLimited, config via env (index.ts intEnv pattern), aur ek mutation row.

question: What do the RD and RA bits mean, and why does the stub server copy the ID and RD while upstream queries are sent with RD=0?
answer_hinglish:
RD (recursion desired) client set karta hai: "mere liye poora kaam karo, root se answer tak". RA (recursion available) server reply mein set karta hai: "haan, main recursion karta hoon". Stub clients (nslookup, OS resolver) hamesha RD=1 bhejte hain -- interop test mein captured nslookup packets bhi RD=1 hain.

Hamara stub server recursive resolver hai, toh har reply mein ra: true. Client ka RD as is copy hota hai, aur ID bhi -- client apni query ko reply se ID se match karta hai, bilkul jaise hum upstream matchesQuery mein karte hain. ID copy na ho toh client reply ko pehchanega hi nahi; mutation S5 (ID copy hataya) ne 4 tests tod diye, kyunki lagbhag har server test ID check karta hai. AA (authoritative answer) false hai, kyunki hum zone ke owner nahi.

Upstream ki taraf ulta: Resolver.exchange buildQuery(randomId(), name, type, false) se RD=0 bhejta hai. Iterative resolution mein hum khud root -> TLD -> zone chalte hain; authoritative servers se recursion nahi maangte. RD=1 bhejne par kuch servers (jo open resolver bhi hain) poora kaam karke de dete, aur hum unke cache par bharosa kar rahe hote -- bailiwick aur hamari apni checks ka matlab khatam. Test 'follows root -> test -> alpha.test referrals using glue, with RD=0 on every query' fake servers ke log mein har query ka rd false check karta hai; mutation R10 (queries sent with RD=1) isi ne pakda.
why_needed: RD/RA stub vs recursive vs authoritative ke roles ka sabse seedha signal hai; interviewers yahi se shuru karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Travel agent (recursive) ko aap kehte ho 'poora trip book karo' (RD=1). Agent airline aur hotel ko seedha phone karta hai aur unse sirf apne hisse ki baat poochta hai (RD=0).
how_it_works: client RD=1, ID=x -> server: reply ID=x, QR=1, RD=1, RA=1, AA=0. Server -> upstream: RD=0, ID=random -> referral/answer.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handle ka base(): id: header.id, rd: header.rd, ra: true, aa: false. src/resolver.ts exchange: buildQuery(randomId(), name, type, false). Tests: server.test.ts 'answers an A query: same ID, QR and RA set, RD copied, question echoed'; resolver.test.ts RD=0 test.
advantages: Roles saaf: stub server recursive, upstream iterative
ID echo se client matching
RD=0 se hum kisi aur ke cache par depend nahi
disadvantages: Client RD=0 bheje tab bhi hum recurse karte hain (RD sirf copy hota hai, behaviour nahi badalta)
common_mistakes: Upstream ko RD=1 bhejna
Reply mein AA=1 set karna
Client ka ID copy na karna
follow_up_questions: Client RD=0 bheje toh RFC ke hisaab se kya karna chahiye?
Forwarder mode mein upstream RD kya hoga?
